title: story-047 pools ALL clients' set-aside buffers into one global setAsideBufferRecipient: in a multi-client deployment every non-recipient client's dip-absorption reserve is silently routed to the single recipient, while stale story-042 NatSpec still promises a per-client reserve
additionalLocations: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:353-372 (single aggregate safeTransfer to setAsideBufferRecipient — source-verified)
description: Since story-047, the set-aside buffer is never returned to the contributing client — _distributeBuffer sums all clients' set-asides and sends the aggregate in a single safeTransfer to the global setAsideBufferRecipient. The implementation is FAITHFUL to story-047 and conservation holds (Tier-3 bufferConservation PASS). The hazard is DISTRIBUTIONAL inside the protocol's own books: in a multi-client deployment, a non-recipient client whose underwater-exit machinery expects its own buffer back (the superseded story-042 semantics, still promised by the setAsideBufferSize NatSpec at AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 and IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132) finds its reserve silently subsidizing the recipient, and its underwater withdrawals can revert for lack of buffer. The per-client setSetAsideBuffer setter shape plus the stale NatSpec actively teach the owner the wrong model.
impact: No value leaves the protocol (realized SURPLUS only is redirected; principal accounting untouched; conservation verified). In a future multi-client deployment with multi-client nonzero buffer config, a non-recipient client's availability assumption is broken until manually rebalanced — funds sit at the recipient, not lost. No external attacker exists anywhere in the path.
attackPath: 1. (Owner config, future multi-client deployment) Owner authorizes two or more clients on one strategy and sets nonzero setAsideBufferSize for more than one of them — plausible because setSetAsideBuffer is per-client and its NatSpec still describes a per-client reserve.
2. Owner sets setAsideBufferRecipient to the address serving client A (e.g. stable-staker's buffer).

3. On every skimSurplus, _distributeBuffer sums ALL clients' set-asides and transfers the aggregate to the single recipient (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:368); client B's dip-absorption reserve never reaches client B.

4. Client B's underwater-exit path, sized against the documented story-042 reserve, reverts or under-delivers when the dip arrives. Funds are not lost — they sit at the recipient — but B's availability assumption is broken until manually rebalanced.
5. No external attacker exists anywhere in this path; every actor is the owner or a protocol-owned client.
lawBasis: Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun (FAITH-15-006 independently retained the same footgun at Low). Surprise test PASSES: the per-client setSetAsideBuffer setter and its NatSpec actively teach the owner the wrong model. NOT an unsafe story (Law-1/Law-2 check passed in FAITH-15-006): the implementation is FAITHFUL to story-047, redirect is explicit and loudly documented on the recipient side, and story-047 actually removes the old front-run-the-skim self-benefit incentive.
documentationCheck: NOT-BLESSED. knownIssuesCount=0. No designDecision mentions a buffer recipient or cross-client routing (story-047 postdates the registry extraction of 2026-01-23). The AUDITOR NOTE at AYieldStrategy.sol:325-335 blesses the adjacent deposit-weighting quirk, not cross-client recipient routing. No systemAssumption covers multi-client buffer configuration.
tier3Evidence: bufferConservation PASS under forge (256x250) and Medusa (200k tests): totalSetAside <= underlyingReceived, exact two-transfer split, dust to skim recipient. Distributional only; no value creation or leak.
recommendation: Safe config: set nonzero setAsideBufferSize ONLY for the client that is (or funnels to) the setAsideBufferRecipient; consider an on-chain guard rejecting nonzero buffers for clients other than the recipient's funnel, or making the recipient per-client. Fix stale NatSpec at AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 and IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132 to state buffers are protocol-level yield routing to setAsideBufferRecipient, not client reserves (F-04, single combined doc-fix item with FAITH-15-003).
